findings.description: Audit point 1 verified: Ordinary issue create/update cannot attach the reserved `projection:autopilot-phase` marker. `_reject_reserved_projection_label` runs before any DB call in `IssueService.create` (issue_service.py:274) and `IssueService.update` (issue_service.py:425). Ordinary update/close mutate only through `mutate_issue_if_unowned` RPC which takes `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, refuses registry-owned UUIDs (`projection_issue_immutable`) and reserved markers before allowlisted UPDATE. All four HTTP entry points (POST /issues/create, /issues/update, /issues/close, PATCH /issues/{id}/labels) map `ProjectionIssueMutationError` to HTTP 403. Round 16 atomic batch close (`close_issues_if_unowned`) locks complete batch in stable UUID order, validates all members before any mutation, all-or-none semantics. Verified by live test `test_issue_service_batch_close_is_atomic_across_projection_boundary`.

Audit point 2 verified: Migration 039 projection RPCs insert unlabelled row, register UUID in `work_queue_projection_ownership`, then apply exact canonical label pair transactionally (039:158-193). Trigger `enforce_projection_label_ownership` (039:398-417) rejects post-migration unowned inserts/label updates with `reserved_projection_label` (ERRCODE 42501). First-insert SSE driven by migration 037 `notify_work_queue_change` on label UPDATE (037:75-110), not inert insert trigger. Replay, concurrent serialization, and explicit admin adoption of pre-039 rows via `INSERT INTO work_queue_projection_ownership` all work. Verified by live tests `test_039_upgrade_fails_closed_until_owner_registers_verified_row` and `test_connected_sse_refreshes_for_first_canonical_projection_insert`.

Audit point 3 verified: Keyed submit and reconcile authorize `publish_work_projection` in service layer with exact `change_id` resource and audit context `{mode: submit|reconcile, change_id}` (work_queue.py:777-800, 922-933). Direct MCP/service callers invoke same service methods; no fallback to ordinary `submit_work` check. `publish_work_projection` gated by trust-level-3 via native policy (`ADMIN_ACTIONS`), Cedar schema/policy, and migration 039 profile backfill. Test `test_standard_trust_cannot_publish_projection` pins HTTP 403.

Audit point 4 verified: Cedar policy mode resolves omitted trust through shared fail-closed `resolve_trust_level` (cedar_policy_engine.py:85-120, 735-752). `TrustResolutionError` becomes `PolicyDecision.deny("trust_resolution_failed: ...")` before policy load or Cedar evaluation, mirroring native engine. Denials surface as `failure_category="policy"` in submit/reconcile before RPC. Guardrail block re-raises `TrustResolutionError` instead of swallowing (work_queue.py:880-885, 972-973).

Audit point 5 verified: In-process `converge()` resolves vendor panel via `_orchestrator_for_dispatch(None, worktree_path)` (convergence_loop.py:610-616) using reviewed `worktree_path`. Resolver precedence: explicit `agents_yaml` > reviewed checkout local `agents.yaml` > coordinator > global disk (review_dispatcher.py:2575-2592). Falls back past coordinator only when both `adapters` and `sdk_adapters` empty, preserving SDK-only coordinator rosters. Verified by tests `test_converge_resolves_vendor_panel_from_reviewed_worktree` and `test_dispatch_preserves_sdk_only_coordinator_roster`.

Audit point 6 verified: Labelled and legacy unlabelled modes isolated in both directions before head/row mutation. Unlabelled requests against any registry-owned row return `projection_mode_mismatch` (039:128-135 submit, 279-286 reconcile). Labelled requests against any complete unowned keyed row return `projection_key_collision` (039:113-127 submit, 264-278 reconcile). Exact-key replay of owned row dedups via ON CONFLICT and re-applies labels (039:160-193). Newer-generation labelled reconcile cancels only owned active rows and clears their labels (039:344-362). Unlabelled reconcile preserves historical tuple cancellation (039:332-342) only when no owned/reserved-labelled state exists. Head upserted only after all preflights (039:326-329). Pre-039 upgrade pinned by fresh-migration tests.

Audit point 7 verified: Direct MCP (`coordination_mcp.py:330-367,408-428`) and HTTP-proxy (`http_proxy.py:481-530`) accept and forward exact `projection_labels` pair. Every projection conflict maps to structured HTTP 409 via `_PROJECTION_CONFLICTS` set in `coordination_api.py:95-101` rather than trigger exceptions. Tests `test_projection_key_collision_maps_to_conflict` and `test_projection_conflict_returns_409_problem` pin this.

Audit point 8 verified: Every HTTP issue-mutation entry point including `PATCH /issues/{issue_id}/labels` catches `ProjectionIssueMutationError` and maps both `projection_issue_immutable` and `reserved_projection_label` to HTTP 403 while preserving row (coordination_api.py:3267-3273). For owned row, service-level reserved-label guard fires before RPC (current labels carry marker). For removal-only patch, RPC returns `projection_issue_immutable` after locking row before UPDATE. Parameterized test `test_patch_issue_labels_maps_projection_refusal_to_forbidden` asserts status 403 and `detail == reason` for both reasons.

Audit point 9 verified: `mutate_issue_if_unowned` checks locked row's existing labels for reserved marker (039:438-440) and patch labels (039:441-446), returns structured `reserved_projection_label` before UPDATE statement at 039:448. UPDATE OF labels ownership trigger never reached for unowned pre-registry reserved row. Live test `test_039_issue_mutation_fails_closed_on_reserved_upgrade_row` applies non-label `{"status": "completed"}` patch to pre-039 spoof row, asserts structured reason plus unchanged `status='pending'` and labels.

Audit point 10 verified: First-generation SSE visibility on owned labelled path driven by migration 037 `notify_work_queue_change` on label UPDATE (037:75-110) after migration 039 stages insert and ownership. Migration 039 inserts are intentionally unlabelled; `notify_projection_insert` trigger (039:468-498, AFTER INSERT gated on marker) never fires for labelled RPC path because BEFORE INSERT ownership trigger rejects marked inserts. Reactivation adds explicit notify (039:374-384). Documentation in design.md:27, change-context.md D5, tasks.md 2.7, and operator guide correctly attribute first event to migration-037 UPDATE; behaviour and documentation agree.

Audit point 11 verified: `PATCH /issues/{issue_id}/labels` declares HTTP 403 response for `projection_issue_immutable` and `reserved_projection_label` in openspec/contracts/agent-coordinator/openapi/kanban-viz.yaml:113-125. Executable contract test `test_patch_issue_labels_maps_projection_refusal_to_forbidden` (test_kanban_viz_endpoints.py:490-519) parametrizes both reasons and pins 403 with `detail == reason`.

Audit point 12 verified: Upgrade guidance consistently requires explicit provenance verification and adoption of every complete keyed row for a change, including cancelled historical generations. Migration 039 table COMMENT (039:37-41): 'adopt every verified keyed row for the change'. Design.md:74: 'insert every verified complete keyed row UUID for that change'. Operator guide (docs/guides/work-queue-truth-projection.md:150): 'enumerate every complete keyed row... verify each row provenance... insert every verified UUID... Cancelled historical generations remain part of this fail-closed set; adopting only the current row is insufficient'. Runtime labelled preflight at 039:113-127 (submit) and 264-278 (reconcile) returns `projection_key_collision` whenever any unowned row with complete projection tuple exists for the change, regardless of status.

Audit point 13 verified: Round 16 blocker closed end-to-end. `IssueService.close` calls single `close_issues_if_unowned` RPC with complete ID batch. RPC locks all existing issue members in stable UUID order (`ORDER BY issue.id FOR UPDATE` at 039:482), detects registry-owned or reserved-labelled members before any UPDATE (039:484-494), leaves every ordinary member unchanged on refusal, returns successful rows in request order via `jsonb_agg(to_jsonb(issue) ORDER BY requested.ordinal)` for PostgREST-compatible JSONB and direct asyncpg client (039:495-501). Missing/duplicate IDs preserve prior skip/ordering behavior (unnest with ordinality). Non-issue tasks excluded by `task_type='issue'` join condition. Live test `test_issue_service_batch_close_is_atomic_across_projection_boundary` proves all-or-none across projection boundary; raw SQL regression in `test_fresh_database_migration.py` validates ordering and atomicity.

Minor: Stale migration attribution in operator guide (docs/guides/work-queue-truth-projection.md:85-90) references migration 038 for atomic label apply and head repair, but at HEAD migration 039 drops and redefines both RPCs (039:43-44, 217-218); 038's versions inserted labelled rows directly with no ownership registry. Later paragraphs correctly credit 039. Internally inconsistent sentence could misdirect operator to wrong migration when reasoning about label staging.

Minor: Direct-transport MCP `issue_update` and `issue_close` (coordination_mcp.py:716-720, 768-772) do not handle `ProjectionIssueMutationError`; it falls into blanket `except Exception` which logs full stack trace at ERROR and returns `reason: "ProjectionIssueMutationError: projection_issue_immutable"`. Refusal still enforced (RPC never mutates), but expected policy refusal reported as internal failure with prefixed reason, unlike HTTP 403 and proxy transport's `{"error": "http_403", "detail": {...}}` envelope.

Minor: Behavioural narrowing in `mutate_issue_if_unowned` selects `WHERE id=p_issue_id AND task_type='issue'` (039:426-428), returns `issue_not_found` otherwise. Previously `IssueService.update`/`close` used `db.update("work_queue", match={"id": ...})` with no task-type filter, so caller passing ordinary task UUID to `/issues/update`, `/issues/close`, or MCP `issue_close` could mutate it; at HEAD such calls return `None`/HTTP 404 (update) or silently drop id from batch (close). Tighter contract is arguably correct for issue API but unannounced compatibility change for operator scripts.

Test coverage gap: No live PostgreSQL test drives `IssueService.update`/`close` through `mutate_issue_if_unowned` and back through `_issue_from_mutation_result` and `Issue.from_row` on `to_jsonb(v_issue)` payload. RPC exercised only via raw SQL in `test_fresh_database_migration.py` and service only against `AsyncMock` rows. Static reading shows round-trip should work (jsonb renders timestamptz as ISO-8601 with `+00:00`, UUIDs/arrays become strings/lists), but successful mutation path with real column types unpinned.

Dead code: `try_projection_issue_list` and `try_projection_issue_update` (coordination_bridge.py:822-870) have no production caller (only tests reference them). `try_projection_issue_update` posts to `/issues/update` with labels patch, which at HEAD is refused with HTTP 403 for every registry-owned row, so helper can no longer do what docstring says. Dead code documenting now-forbidden path is trap for future caller.

Minor: Operator guide (docs/guides/work-queue-truth-projection.md:205) says reactivated projection issue becomes "visible and executable again," but migration 037 categorically excludes every `task_type=issue` row from claims (037:28-30). Same guide later calls these rows unclaimable. Recovery description internally contradictory.

Minor: Upgrade guidance wording on cancelled historical generations uneven across surfaces. Operator guide (docs/guides/work-queue-truth-projection.md:150) explicitly requires adoption of cancelled generations. Design.md:74 and table COMMENT (039:37-41) require every verified keyed/complete keyed row but omit cancelled/only-current warning; preamble at 039:34-36 says singular "the row id". Runtime fail-closes on any unowned complete keyed row (039:113-127, 264-278), so behavior correct; only explicit cancelled-generation wording uneven.

Minor: Migration 039 header comment (line 1) says 'notify first labelled inserts' which contradicts corrected first-generation attribution to migration-037 labelled UPDATE path and inert insert-trigger reality on owned labelled RPC path. Durable design/operator docs already correct.

Minor: `PATCH /issues/{id}/labels` against registry-owned projection row refused with detail `reserved_projection_label` rather than `projection_issue_immutable` in common case: `show()` returns owned row's current labels including marker, route merges add/remove, `IssueService.update` Python precheck (issue_service.py:425) rejects retained marker before RPC reports ownership. Only request explicitly removing marker reaches RPC and surfaces `projection_issue_immutable`. Both map to 403 and row untouched; unit test parametrizes both reasons via mock rather than exercising which live path emits.

Minor: Implicit cancelled-row exclusion in `IssueService.list_issues` is asymmetric: applies only when labels supplied and status is None (issue_service.py:107-110). Status-less, label-less list still returns cancelled rows (no status filter appended), while same call with labels hides them. Board and SSE snapshot always pass labels so defense-in-depth goal met, but API consumers see two different default status sets for one endpoint.
